itemized.notes: 4-page filing whose pages are OUT OF THE FORM'S OWN ORDER: PDF p1 is the cover, PDF p2 is Schedule B (its page box reads 'Page 1 of 3'), PDF p3 is Schedule A ('Page 2 of 3'), and the Summary Page is PDF p4 ('Page 3 of 3') - i.e. the filer numbered the two schedules ahead of the summary and the scan preserved that order, so Schedule B precedes Schedule A in the document. BOTH SCHEDULES ARE GENUINELY BLANK, and that is a real zero rather than a gap: the pre-printed grids are present and complete, no data row on either page carries a date, name, address, occupation, purpose or amount, and the filer signed the account off with hand-drawn zero glyphs. Per the repo ZERO-GLYPH RULING those drawn glyphs denote 0 and are read as 0 - but they sit in the SUBTOTAL and TOTAL cells, which are not itemized lines, so no contribution or expenditure row is emitted for them. ONE THING A HUMAN MAY WANT TO LOOK AT, recorded rather than resolved: on each schedule the AMOUNT cell of the very FIRST otherwise-empty data row also carries a hand-drawn zero-shaped glyph (on Schedule A it reads more like a doubled 'OO'). Those are not itemized lines - the row has no date, no name and no purpose - so nothing was transcribed from them; they are most plausibly the filer stroking a zero through the first row to say 'none', but that is an inference and is stated as one, not written into a field.
